**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 9 already delivers our preferred T4C position without amendment:

| Playbook element | Document | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Customer convenience right | § 9.4 — Agreement *and* any Order Form | Met |
| 30 days' notice | § 29.4 — thirty days | Met |
| Pro-rata refund of prepaid fees | § 9.4 — accrued Fees only + refund | Met |
| No early-termination fee | None in §§ 7, 9, 10 | Met |
| No Vendor mid-term convenience right | Only for-cause (§§ 9.1, 9.2) | Met |

Two points worth noting for the wider review, outside this rule's scope:

1. **§ 9.4 relies on a remote cross-reference.** The 30-day period sits in the Notices section (§ 29.4) rather than in the termination clause itself. It is legally effective as drafted, so I did not flag it — but if you want belt-and-braces protection against a future amendment to § 29 inadvertently diluting our exit right, stating "thirty (30) days' prior written notice" directly in § 9.4 would be a cheap, non-controversial tidy-up.
2. **§ 7.7 is a genuinely aggressive term.** It imposes "fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week" an invoice remains unpaid, labelled liquidated damages. That compounds to an extreme figure and is likely unenforceable as a penalty, but it is a payment-terms issue rather than an early-termination charge, so it does not affect this rule's outcome. It should be picked up under the payment/late-fee rule if one is in scope.
